name: Aegis of the Founding Stone
text: A shield cut from the town's cornerstone. Raised once per siege, it makes every wall and gate unbreakable for a full minute.

name: Arrowstorm Quiver
text: Each arrow drawn from it splits into three in flight. A tower archer wearing it covers a whole stretch of wall alone.

name: Banner of the Free City
text: Flown from the town hall, the banner lifts the mood of every citizen and makes defenders refuse to break while it stands.

name: Skull Ring of the Barrow-King
text: A bone ring carved as a grinning skull, taken from a barrow-king's finger. The dead hesitate before striking whoever wears it.

name: Beacon Sceptre
text: An iron rod capped with a beacon-lamp's lens. Raised, it throws a hard light, and brawlers and bullies back down.

name: Bell of the Long Night
text: A black iron bell for the temple tower. While it tolls during a siege, undead attackers move slowly and the weakest crumble outright.

name: Bloodmoss Poultice
text: The alchemist's cheapest seller: pressed onto a wound it stops bleeding at once and knits a little flesh, so heroes keep fighting instead of limping home.

name: Blue-Eye Bead
text: A cobalt glass bead painted like an eye. It turns aside envious glances and the evil eye; it shatters when it saves its wearer.
inspiredBy: Middle Eastern and Mediterranean folk custom

name: Boar-Splitter Maul
text: A heavy maul carved with a broken tusk. It strikes orcs hard enough to stagger them, and Bloodtusk raiders single out whoever carries it.

name: Bounty Board Seal
text: Bounties stamped with this wax seal are heard of in distant towns, drawing wandering heroes who would never otherwise come.

name: Bountysworn Blade
text: This sword grows keener every day its wielder spends chasing a posted bounty, and goes dull if they wander off for loot instead.

name: Broken Warlord Tusk
text: Taken from a fallen warchief and nailed above the town gate, it makes orc warbands hesitate before attacking and some turn back altogether.

name: Burghers' Seven-Link Chain
text: Seven heavy links, one for each guild that swore to the League. Councillors who see it on the mayor remember their oaths.

name: Caravan Bell
text: Hung from a lead wagon, its tone makes wolves and wild beasts shy away from the road. Bandits, sadly, are not beasts.

name: Chain of the First Charter
text: Brass links strung with the wax seal of the town's charter. Whoever wears it speaks for the town, and a hall listens a little longer.

name: Chieftain Cleaver
text: A greataxe that hits leaders hardest. When it fells a warband's chief, the rest of the band breaks and scatters.

name: Compass Crown
text: A circlet with a needle at its brow. Once a season it lifts the fog from the whole map for a day, and its wearer's council cannot be bought.

name: Compass of the Lost Road
text: The needle points home. A party carrying it can always retreat to town and never loses its way in the fog.

name: Concealed Shoe
text: A child's worn shoe walled up beside the chimney. Malicious spirits are drawn into it and trapped, so the building shrugs off the first haunting or curse each season.
inspiredBy: English and Northern European folk custom

name: Councillor's Signet
text: Lets the wearer sense lies spoken in the council chamber. Councillors who sell secrets avoid whoever wears it.

name: Courtier's Rapier
text: A slender rapier with a jewelled guard, quicker in the hand than it looks. More duels are won with it in the first three passes than in the next thirty.

name: Cucumber Offering
text: A basket of cucumbers with the family name carved into each. Tossed into a river before a crossing, it buys one caravan safe passage past kappa and other river spirits.

name: Daisy-Wheel Marks
text: Overlapping compass circles scratched into the beams and lintels of a tavern or barn. Wandering spirits get lost tracing the endless lines and never reach the people inside.

name: Dawnspear of the First Mayor
text: The spear the town was founded around. Its point burns with morning light that destroys undead, and its bearer can lay a lich low.

name: Dawnwatch Whetstone
text: A few strokes give a blade a bright edge that bites harder for the rest of the day. Wears down after a dozen uses.

name: Dragonscale Ring
text: A ring of overlapping red scales, still warm. Blows aimed at its wearer slide off as if they hit a dragon's flank.

name: Lantern of the Drowned Road
text: A green-glassed lantern salvaged from a sunken causeway. Its light lays a road of solid mist over still water for as long as it burns.

name: Duelist's Estoc
text: A long, stiff thrusting blade with no edge to speak of. It finds the gaps between plates and the gaps in a guard.

name: Elixir of Bold Return
text: Drunk automatically when the hero is close to death, it heals them a little and sends them sprinting home at double speed.

name: Emberroot Tonic
text: A peppery draught that keeps a hero warm through a winter night. Parties carrying it ignore cold-weather slowdowns on mountain roads for a day.

name: Enchanter's Ley Loupe
text: A crystal eyepiece for the enchanting shop. Seeing exactly where the ley flows in a crystal, the enchanter wastes far less of it on each item.

name: Eye of the Sleepless Spire
text: A crystal eye set atop the mage tower. Everything within a day's ride of town is shown live, always, with no scryer to pay.

name: Far-Seeing Basin
text: A silver basin for the mage tower. Once a day it shows one site under fog as it is right now, without paying a scryer.

rt.fog: daily live view of one site

name: Ferryman's Coin
text: An old copper with a boat on one face. Toss it in any river and the water calms enough for its owner to wade across, if they keep walking and never look down.

name: Fire-Gem Ring
text: A gold ring set with a gem that holds a living flame. Its wearer's spells and blades carry a little of the fire with them.

name: Gatebreaker Ram Head
text: An iron ram head carved with a boar. Warbands mount it on a ram; it shatters ordinary gates in a few blows. Captured, it can be melted into relic fragments.

name: Ghostcap Draught
text: Brewed from pale mushrooms, it lets the drinker see spirits and invisible things for a minute. Tastes like a cellar.

name: Ghostlight Drops
text: Two drops in the eyes and cult sigils hidden under sleeves and collars glow faintly. Watchmen use them to sweep a district for infiltrators.

name: Goatfoot Crampons
text: Iron spikes cut like a goat's hooves. Strapped on, they carry their wearer up a sheer cliff face as if it were a stair.

name: Grey Pilgrim's Cloak
text: Its wearer looks like a harmless traveller. Scouts slip past orc pickets and through enemy camps without starting a fight.

name: Guild Charter
text: A sealed charter granting a guild rights in town. Whoever holds it can open a guildhall without a council vote.

name: Hagstone
text: A pebble with a hole worn through by water. Looking through it shows a shapechanger's true form, so a sentry carrying one can unmask an aswang or kelpie in the crowd.

name: Hearth Saucer
text: A clay dish set out each night with milk and bread. A household that keeps one is helped by its house spirit: fewer fires, healthier animals, a little more output.

name: Heartstone of the Keep
text: Set in the foundation of the keep, it lets damaged walls slowly regrow between assaults, so a siege must break them all at once.

name: Highland Claymore
text: A great two-handed sword as tall as a halfling. It keeps a ring of foes at bay with its reach, and few stand to meet its swing.

name: Honest Ledger
text: False figures written in this book fade before the ink is dry. A market keeping its accounts in it loses nothing to crooked traders.

name: Horse-Brass Harness
text: Polished brass plates that flash on a draft horse's harness. Caravan teams wearing them do not spook at black dogs, will-o-wisps or the cries of roadside spirits.

name: Horse-Lord's Sabre
text: A curved cavalry sabre that sings when it is swung from the saddle, and cuts deepest at a gallop.

name: Horseshoe Over the Door
text: An old iron shoe nailed points-up above a doorway. Fey and household spirits cannot cross that threshold uninvited, and the house keeps its luck.

name: Iron Hammer Pendant
text: A small forged hammer on a leather cord. Trolls and restless dead hesitate before its wearer, and lightning never strikes the house it hangs in.

name: Ironbark Harness
text: Armour grown by druids from living bark. It is as tough as chain, and slowly closes its wearer's wounds while they stand in sunlight.

name: Lamplighter's Wick
text: A street lamp fitted with this wick burns for a month without oil. Lit streets see fewer thefts and fewer cultist meetings.

name: Last-Sheaf Dolly
text: A figure woven from the final sheaf of the harvest and hung in the granary until spring. Field spirits are appeased, noon-day harvest attacks stop and next year's yield improves.
inspiredBy: British and Central European harvest custom

name: Lichbane Lantern
text: Its cold flame leans toward the nearest phylactery, and lesser undead caught in its light smoulder and flee.

name: Living Campaign Map
text: A map table that redraws itself as parties report in. Lairs that have been seen show a rough guess of how much their monsters have grown since.

name: Lodestone Ring of Recall
text: Twisting it pulls the wearer and anyone holding their hand back to the town square. It works once, then needs a week in the temple to recharge.

name: Falchion of the Low Road
text: A heavy, single-edged falchion made for chopping through brush and bandits alike. It hits hardest on a downward stroke.

name: Lych-Gate Bell
text: A cracked bronze bell hung over the graveyard gate. It rings on its own whenever something dead walks out, waking the watch and showing where the restless grave lies.

name: Mantle of the Lamplit Hall
text: Midnight wool stitched with the old temple lamps. Its wearer recalls the right old story at the right time.

name: Mapmaker's Ink
text: Maps drawn in this ink do not smudge in rain or blood. A party's report of what it saw stays accurate on the town map twice as long.

name: Militia Armband
text: A stitched band of the town colours. Peasants called to the walls while wearing it hold their nerve a little longer before breaking.

name: Muster Standard
text: A war standard raised over the gate when companies ride out. They fight under it, and come back to it.

name: Nightwatch Brigandine
text: Dark leather riveted with iron. A guard wearing it on the walls at night spots climbers and sappers long before they arrive.

name: Oathbound Chain
text: Forged from the fetters of a broken tyrant. It warms when its wearer is lied to and steadies the voice when it matters.

name: Orrery of the Unseen Roads
text: Brass rings that trace every road in the region. It shows where caravans are and lights up red wherever an ambush waits.

name: Outer Wall Alarm Bell
text: Mounted on a tower, it rings by itself when an armed band comes within a mile, and marks the band's size on the map.

name: Pack Mule Harness
text: Any beast in this harness carries half again its load without slowing. Caravans fitted with a set return with more goods.

name: Paper Seal Talisman
text: A strip of paper brushed with a binding prayer. Pasted over a door, well cover or shuttered window, it bars spirits and yokai from passing for a week.

name: Plaguebane Cordial
text: Cures any sickness and keeps the drinker immune for a season. Poured into a well, it protects a whole district for a week instead.

name: Plate of the Last Wall
text: While its wearer stands on the town walls they cannot be moved or frightened, and the defenders near them refuse to give ground.

name: Potion of Fog-Walking
text: For an hour the drinker's party moves through unexplored land at road speed and leaves no tracks for monsters to follow.

name: Potion of Second Wind
text: Instantly refills a hero's stamina. Cowardly heroes buy it in pairs so they can always outrun what they fled from.

name: Ring of a Hundred Voices
text: The mayor wearing it can speak to any hero on the map. Once a week, one hero must obey a direct order instead of choosing their own path.

name: Ring of the Quiet Purse
text: The wearer's coin cannot be picked or cut. The thieves' guild keeps a list of who wears these and takes it personally.

name: Road-Worn Mantle
text: A travelling cloak patched by every company that ever wintered in town. Heroes see one of their own in the mayor who wears it.

name: Rod of the Free Market
text: Planted in the market square, it draws caravans from far kingdoms. Every caravan that trades there pays a small tithe to the treasury.

name: Rod of the Ley Diviner
text: It tugs toward buried ley crystals. A party carrying it marks crystal deposits on the map as they pass through the fog.

name: Rowan Cross
text: Two rowan twigs bound with red thread. The wearer sees through fey glamours, and enchanting spells from fey and hags slide off them.

name: Rumor Pipe
text: Smoke from this clay pipe loosens tongues around a tavern table. The tavern that owns one turns up an extra rumor each week.

name: Rune-Lit Ring
text: A plain iron band whose runes glow blue when a lie is spoken nearby, and burn when a trap is close.

name: Running-Water Ring
text: A blessed stone channel that diverts a stream all the way around the town walls. Undead, the nuckelavee and other things that fear fresh flowing water cannot cross it.

name: Sacred Straw Rope
text: A thick twisted rope hung with paper streamers, tied around a well, shrine tree or boundary stone. Spirits treat what lies inside as holy ground and leave it alone.

name: Saddle Pocket
text: A leather pocket no bigger than a purse that holds one horse, saddle and all. Whistle into it at a ford and the horse steps out onto the far bank with its rider already up.

name: Sceptre of Quiet Courts
text: Tapped once on the floor, it hushes a room. Quarrels in the hall end sooner, and the town feels a firm hand.

name: Scroll of Distant Eyes
text: When read in the town hall it opens a live window onto one region of the map for an hour, showing everything moving there.

rt.fog: one-hour live view of a region

name: Scroll of Patched Stone
text: Pressed against a cracked wall section, it fills the breach with rough stone in seconds. Masons stockpile them before siege season.

name: Scroll of Sending Word
text: Read aloud, it carries one short message from a party in the fog back to the town hall, without spending anyone's spell slots.

name: Scroll of the Great Cleansing
text: Read from the temple steps, it burns a plague out of the whole town in a single night and drives away rats that carry it.

name: Scroll of the Sealed Report
text: A report written on it reaches the mayor unread and unaltered, so a cultist courier cannot twist what the party saw.

name: Seal of the Unbroken Word
text: A carnelian seal said to crack if its owner breaks a promise. The townsfolk trust a mayor who wears it whole.

name: Self-Swinging Sword
text: A treasure sword from old Russian tales that leaps from its scabbard and fights alone. Hung on the town wall in a siege, it duels any dragon, giant or champion that approaches.

name: Sending Stone Pair
text: Two river stones cut from one, each carved with the same knot. Whoever holds one can speak a few words into it and be heard by whoever holds the other, however far apart they are. The town keeps one half in the hall and gives the other to a company on the road.

name: Shield of the Narrow Gate
text: A tall door-shaped shield. A hero holding a gate or bridge with it cannot be pushed back, and enemies pile up in front of them.

name: Signet of the Open Hand
text: An open palm cut in silver. Adventurers who take a commission sealed with it feel the town keeps faith with them.

name: Spiked River Plate
text: Plate armor bristling with blades, made to fight a great worm in a river. Any creature that coils around or swallows the wearer is cut apart, and it never rusts.

name: Staff of the Hedge Warden
text: Thorny hedges burst from the ground where it points, snaring raiders who come for the town's outlying farms.

name: Staff of the Plague Warden
text: A healer walking a district with this staff burns away sickness in the air. One quarter of town can be cleared of plague each day.

name: Surveyor's Chain
text: A brass measuring chain that lays itself out straight. Land plots surveyed with it are ready to build on in half the time.

name: Tavern Tally Stick
text: Notches itself whenever a hero runs up a tab. No hero can skip town owing the tavern, and the tavern's takings rise.

name: Toll-Free Coin
text: A coin stamped on both sides with a road. Paid at any toll gate it is accepted and then vanishes, letting one caravan pass free.

name: Town Pennant
text: The town's colours on a lance pennon, handed to each company as it marches. They strike harder carrying it.

name: Turned-Coat Charm
text: A stitched patch reminding travelers to wear their coats inside out when the path starts to loop. A party that does breaks any trail-twisting spell and finds its way home on time.

name: Twin Scrying Pebbles
text: A scout drops one pebble at a site in the fog; the other, kept in town, shows a single glimpse of that spot when rubbed. Then both go dull.

rt.fog: one later glimpse of a marked site

name: Unveiling Mirror
text: Hung in the council chamber, it shows each week whose reflection bears a cult mark. Infiltrators start finding reasons to skip meetings.

name: Wall Ward Glyph
text: Enchanted from a ley crystal and a relic fragment, a glyph set into a wall section hurls back the first assault on it each siege.

name: Wand of Kindling Flares
text: Fires a slow-falling star that lights a stretch of fog for a few seconds, showing the town map anything standing beneath it.

rt.fog: brief reveal of a small area

name: Wand of Whispered Orders
text: The mayor can whisper a short order into it and the party leader carrying its twin hears it, wherever they are in the fog.

rt.fog: send short orders to one party

name: Warbanner of the Marching Guilds
text: Carried onto the field, it makes heroes of different guilds fight as one company, sharing targets and covering each other's retreats.

name: Wardsalt Mantlet
text: A wheeled wooden screen packed with wardsalt. Archers behind it shrug off arrows, and hostile spells fizzle against its face.

name: Wardsalt Pouch
text: A line of blessed salt poured across a doorway or camp keeps lesser undead from crossing it until dawn.

name: Water-Horse Bridle
text: A silver-studded bridle that, once slipped over a water horse's head, binds it to obey. A caravan hitched to such a horse crosses rivers without a ford.

name: Wax-and-Iron Signet
text: A plain iron ring with a seal that leaves a mark no clerk can copy. Forged letters and false ledgers come to light.

name: Wayfarer's Chalk
text: Marks drawn with it glow for a season. Parties use it to mark safe paths, and later parties follow them faster.

name: Witch Bottle
text: A stoneware jar of bent pins, rosemary and the owner's hair, buried under the hearth. The next curse aimed at the household lodges in the bottle instead, and the jar cracks.

name: Rimecleaver
text: A battleaxe with a double bit of blue ice that never melts. Its edge smokes with cold, and a perfect blow leaves the foe frozen where it stood.

name: Headsman's Drop
text: A heavy-headed axe balanced for one downward stroke. It was made for the block and has never lost the habit.

name: Dicer's Stiletto
text: A slim knife strung with gold beads that click like dice. It turns in the hand as if it wanted to be thrown, and when luck runs its way it runs hard.

name: Sunflare Sabre
text: Its blade is etched with a sunrise. A perfect cut lets loose a flash that leaves the foe blind for a breath.

name: Gravethorn Pike
text: A pike of black wood that grew in a barrow. It drinks the warmth from what it pierces.

name: Farshot Longbow
text: Capped with bronze kestrels and strung with silver gut. Its archer sees the foe first and looses before the ambush is sprung.

name: Rootwoven Bow
text: Its limbs are knotted roots that still put out green shoots in spring. Three times a day an arrow grows wings and finds its mark.

name: Hellforged Trident
text: Three iron tines quenched in a lake of fire. It burns anything that came from the planes above or below.

name: Penitent's Flail
text: Iron knotted on cords, with a stern face on the haft. Its bearer shrugs off the grip of fear and poison by the pain of it.

name: Thunder Maul
text: A stone maul banded in copper. Struck on the ground it lets out a clap that throws a whole rank off its feet.

name: Stormcaller Spear
text: Its head is a sliver of storm-glass. Raised, it calls a bolt that leaps from one foe to the next.

name: Emberbrand
text: A plain sword with a coal-red edge. It is always warm, and it burns where it cuts.

name: Venomfang Kris
text: A wavy dagger with a hollow channel down the blade, cut from a great spider's fang.

name: Wyrmtooth Glaive
text: A dragon's tooth bound to an ash haft. Dragons know it on sight and hate it.

name: Giantsbane Maul
text: A short-hafted maul with a head of meteor iron, made to break knees the height of a door.

name: Ghoulreaper Sickle
text: A silver sickle from a temple's harvest-rite. It cuts the restless dead like ripe wheat and gives their stolen life to its bearer.

name: Leech Blade
text: A dark, narrow sword that sweats red. Every wound it makes closes one of its bearer's.

name: Beastwarden Spear
text: A boar-spear with a cross-bar of horn, carved with the beasts it has stopped.

name: Drumcleaver
text: A warchief's broad axe with a drum-skin wrapped round the haft. When it is raised the weaker of the enemy remember other places to be.

name: Witchfinder's Arbalest
text: A heavy crossbow with a silver stirrup, its bolts dipped in holy salt. It finds fey and hags through any glamour.

name: Plague-Censer Flail
text: A flail whose head is a brass censer of green smoke. What it strikes sickens; its bearer has long since stopped coughing.

name: Drowned King's Trident
text: Barnacled bronze that drips seawater on dry land. It calls the cold of the deep, and lightning from the waves.

name: Clockwork Arbalest
text: A crossbow with a wound spring and a magazine of six bolts. It reloads itself between breaths.

name: Ringmaster's Knife
text: A painted throwing knife from the carnival's knife-act. Its target freezes like a man on a spinning board.

name: Drain-Rat Cleaver
text: A butcher's cleaver gone green with sewer rot. Its wounds fester.

name: Chitin Shortsword
text: A blade of a hive-queen's foreleg, sharper than steel and lighter than bone.

name: Silkbinder Whip
text: Plaited spider silk with a barbed tip. It wraps a foe in a sticky web that holds it fast.

name: False Saint's Mace
text: A gilded mace from a church that lied. Its light is real enough: it sears.

name: Trapper's Catchpole
text: A pole with a noose of enchanted wire, used by beast-traders to take monsters alive.

name: Headless Huntsman's Spear
text: A hunting spear that never stops hunting. Whatever it is pointed at starts to run.

name: Barrow Marshal's Blade
text: A longsword dug from a battlefield where the dead still drill. It remembers every fallen soldier and drinks the living.

name: Thornheart Staff
text: A staff cut from a corrupted grove's heart-tree. Thorns burst from the ground to bind the druid's foes.

name: Tollbreaker Mace
text: A flanged mace from a highway baron's gatehouse, still dented from the last free traveller it met.

name: Laughing Glaive
text: A glaive hung with gnoll teeth that chatter when blood is near. Its bearer fights in a frenzy.

name: Kennel Brand
text: The iron the Ember Kennels heat to mark their hounds. It burns through anything.

name: Smoke-Caller's Staff
text: A staff hung with bone chimes. Its smoke calls the restless dead, and sends them back.

name: Black Bough Bow
text: A longbow of blackened yew from a ranger who turned. It looses two shafts for every one.

name: Forge-Lord's Hammer
text: A smith-king's hammer, still hot from the anvil. Its blows ring like a forge and land like a landslide.

name: Cloud-Lord's Lance
text: A lance of white wood as long as two men, light as a reed. The wind runs ahead of its charge.

name: Storm-King's Harpoon
text: A giant's harpoon cut down to a man's length. Thrown, it brings the storm with it.

name: Oathkeeper's Brand
text: A paladin's longsword whose blade glows brighter the truer its bearer keeps faith.

name: Falling-Star Wraps
text: Hand wraps embroidered with comets. A monk who wears them strikes twice before the first blow lands.

name: Wolfskin Mantle
text: A dire wolf's hide worn as a cloak. In a fury its wearer's wounds close like a wolf's.

name: Thiefcatcher Gloves
text: Black kid gloves taken from a thief-taker. Nothing slips their grip, and nobody slips up behind their wearer.

name: Emberleaf Grimoire
text: A spellbook bound in scorched leather. Read aloud, its first page becomes a fireball.

name: Dragonblood Torc
text: A gold torc with a ruby set in each end. A sorcerer wearing it breathes fire like their forebear.

name: Pact-Chain
text: A fine silver chain whose links whisper the terms of a bargain. Its wearer's patron takes a little life from every foe it touches.

name: Dawn Censer
text: A brass censer that smokes like a sunrise. Its incense mends the faithful.

name: Choirmaster's Lute
text: A lute with a carved mouth for a soundhole. Its chord of command holds a foe spellbound for a verse.

name: Warden's Oakhorn
text: A horn of living oak. Its call makes the forest itself step between the warden and harm.

name: Lodestar Astrolabe
text: A brass astrolabe that always points home. Its maker can send word along the line it draws, and see what waits at the end of the road.

name: Reliquary of the Sleeping Saint
text: A silver box holding a saint's finger-bone. Opened in battle, it turns aside curses and breath alike.

name: Cauldron Charm
text: A thumb-sized iron cauldron on a thong, always simmering. Its hex roots a foe to the spot.

name: Hoarfrost Mail
text: Chain mail furred with frost that never melts. The first foe to strike its wearer freezes to the spot.

name: Runeward Shield
text: A dwarven shield inlaid with living runes that shift when magic comes near. It catches a spell and throws it back.

name: Interposing Shield
text: A tower shield with an eye painted on its boss. It moves on its own to meet the deadliest blow.

name: Dragonhide Plate
text: Plates of a red dragon's hide sewn over steel. Fire runs off it like rain.

name: Salamander-Scale Shield
text: A round shield faced with salamander scales. It drinks heat.

name: Bone-Lattice Armour
text: A coat of bone plates wired together by a necromancer's apprentice. The grave's chill finds no purchase on it.

name: Storm Plate
text: Blue-black plate that crackles in the rain. Lightning bends round its wearer, and bites whoever strikes it.

name: Cloudsilk Mail
text: Mail woven from cloud-giant silk, so light it seems to float. Snares and grapples slide off it.

name: Forgeheart Breastplate
text: A breastplate with a coal glowing behind a grille over the heart. Forge-fire cannot harm its wearer.

name: Hive-Chitin Shield
text: A shield of a hive-warrior's carapace, light and hard as horn.

name: Velvet Brigandine
text: A courtier's padded coat with steel plates sewn in the lining. The borrowed faces wear it under their finery.

name: Witch-Hunter's Coat
text: A long leather coat sewn with iron nails and prayer-strips. Hexes slide off it.

name: Legion Scale
text: Bronze scale from the temple guard of old Caldor, still bright. It holds the line.

name: Blinkstep Gauntlet
text: A silver gauntlet etched with conjuring runes that glow violet when worn. With a pulling motion its wearer steps out of any grip.

name: Torchbearer's Gloves
text: Leather gloves lined with red scales, lines of fire running round the fingers. A torch held in them roars out in a cone of flame.

name: Thundering Greaves
text: Iron greaves too heavy to lift until they are worn. Each stamp is a thunderclap.

name: Amulet of the Steady Heart
text: A ruby heart held in golden hands. Its wearer runs to a fallen friend and mends them twice as well.

name: Rimegrip Gauntlets
text: A frost giant's gauntlets cut down to fit a mortal hand. Their grip is a giant's, and it freezes.

name: Emberheart Belt
text: A fire giant's belt-buckle, a slab of iron with a coal set in it. It lends a forge-lord's strength.

name: Whisperwind Shell
text: One of a pair of spiral shells. Speak into it and the town hall's twin repeats every word.

name: Seer's Glass
text: A palm-sized lens of smoky crystal. Held to the eye, it shows a far place for as long as its holder can bear to look.

name: Hag's Eye
text: A glass eye taken from a hag's coven. It still sees what the coven sees, and what it shows is true.

name: Wolfsbane Charm
text: A bundle of wolfsbane and wolf fangs bound in silver wire. Wolves and things that run with them hate the smell.

name: Troll-Heart Amulet
text: A shrivelled troll's heart in an iron cage, still beating. Its wearer's wounds knit as a troll's do.

name: Spider-Silk Cloak
text: A grey cloak woven by a silk-weaver's whole family over a winter. It cannot be caught on anything.

name: Basilisk-Eye Pendant
text: A basilisk's eye set in lead. Gazes that would petrify its wearer turn back on whoever cast them.

name: Drakescale Ring
text: A ring of overlapping drake scales, warm to the touch.

name: Phylactery Shard
text: A splinter of a lich's soul-vessel, cold and humming. It looses the grave's breath on the living.

name: Demon-Horn Bugle
text: A bugle made from a fiend's curled horn. Its blast sounds like the pit opening, and the weak-hearted flee.

name: Fey-Glass Circlet
text: A circlet of glass leaves from the Court of First Leaves. Its wearer's gaze holds a foe enthralled.

name: Elemental Heartstone
text: The core of a slain elemental, a fist of living storm. Cracked open, it lets the storm out.

name: Ogre-Knuckle Gauntlets
text: Iron gauntlets with an ogre's knuckle-bones set in the backs. Punches land like a cudgel.

name: Spirit Bell
text: A small bronze bell that the dead cannot bear to hear. Rung in a crypt, the restless flee.

name: Black Candle
text: A candle of black tallow from a cult's altar. Lit, its flame is cold and its smoke is death.

name: Gnoll War-Fetish
text: A rattle of bones and hyena hair. It fills its bearer with the pack's hunger.

name: Crown of Teeth
text: A goblin chief's crown of rat teeth and bent nails. Lesser goblins grovel before it, and it bites.

name: War-Drum of the Red Tide
text: A small drum skinned in tattooed hide. Its beat makes allies bolder and enemies run.

name: Death-Mask of the Ninefold Throne
text: A gold funeral mask with lapis eyes. Behind it its wearer cannot be held by any mortal hand, and the dead do not see them.

name: Corsair's Compass
text: A brass compass whose needle points at treasure, not north. Corsairs use it to find ships before ships find them.

name: Caravan Prince's Ring
text: A heavy gold ring with a hidden compartment. Its owner's word travels faster than any caravan.

name: Marcher Lord's Gorget
text: A steel gorget with a house's crest. Its wearer stands like a lord on his own land.

name: Thorn of the Broken Pact
text: A thorn from the rose that bound the Court of First Leaves to its oath. It still pricks oath-breakers.

name: Coil-Whisper Shell
text: A conch from the drowned Coil. Lift it to the ear and hear what the far waters hear.

name: Elderwood Acorn
text: An acorn as big as a fist that hums with the Elder wood's sap. It heals as the forest heals.

name: Key of the Last Door
text: A black iron key that fits no lock in this world. Turned in the air, it opens a door that something answers.

name: Ash Regent's Scale
text: A grey dragon scale the size of a shield, still warm. Fire and fear slide off its bearer.

name: Hollow Choir Hymnal
text: A hymnal whose pages are blank to all but the choir. Its dirge holds the living still.

name: Frost-Sworn Horn
text: A drinking horn rimmed with silver. A jarl's hall-horn, it lends the strength of the long winter.

name: Dawn Gate Shield
text: A kite shield from the Dawn Gate, its face a rising sun. It burns the dead who strike it.

name: Halfling Luck-Penny
text: A copper penny worn thin by a hundred thumbs. Shots aimed with it in a pocket never miss when it matters.

name: Gnomish Flash-Lantern
text: A lantern with a trigger. One squeeze and a blinding flash leaves the nearest foe staggering.

name: Swamp-Spirit Fetish
text: A figure of reeds and crocodile teeth. The swamp's poisons pass its wearer by.

name: Sunclaw
text: A curved claw-blade of the tomb-cats, gilded for a pharaoh's guard. Quick as a cat and sharp as noon.

name: Kestrine Feather Cloak
text: A cloak of the birdfolk's moulted feathers. Its wearer sees from above and is never caught.

name: Sun-Disc of the Oasis
text: A bronze mirror that holds the noon sun. Flashed in a crypt, it burns the dead.

name: Rune-Axe of the Deep Halls
text: A dwarf-king's axe whose runes still glow. It cleaves stone, giants and the things in the deep alike.

name: Moonblade of First Leaves
text: A slender elven blade that shines like the moon on water. It shows the way through any glamour.

name: Harvest-Feast Scythe
text: The scythe the river villages bless at the harvest-feast. In a defender's hands it is a terror.

name: Free Port Cutlass
text: A boarding cutlass with a basket hilt. Its owner gets in two cuts for one.

name: Hollow Legion Spear
text: A bronze spear from Caldor's awakened temple guard. It never tires.

name: Signet of the Pale Lord
text: A ring of black silver taken from a vampire's hand. Whoever wears it feels a knife coming before the hand that holds it moves.

name: Mantle of the Unseen Court
text: Grey velvet worn by the masters of a court of borrowed faces. No charm, glamour or whispered suggestion takes hold of the one inside it.

name: Chain of the True Word
text: A chain of plain iron links, each stamped with an oath. Lies spoken before it catch in the throat, and a turncoat on the council sweats.

name: Sceptre of Iron Silence
text: A giant-king's rod cut down to a man's height. When it strikes the table, the hall falls quiet.

name: Crown of the Drowned King
text: A coral crown hauled up from a sunken throne room. The people bow to it without knowing why, and the sea-wet gems warn of poison in the cup.

name: Circlet of Clear Sight
text: A thin silver band set with a hag's stolen moonstone. Its wearer sees through glamours and borrowed faces.

name: Ninefold Seal
text: A seal of the nine dead kings, cold to the touch. Death itself is slow to find the hand that wears it.

name: Envoy's Ring
text: A ring of plain gold carried by the peoples' envoys. Guests at a table it sits at speak more freely.

name: Taster's Torc
text: A copper torc that turns green when poison is near. Many a merchant prince died for want of one.

name: Banner of the Dragon Pact
text: Dragon-hide painted with a wyrm's sigil. Companies who march under it march as if a dragon were at their backs.

name: Corsairs' Black Flag
text: A tattered black flag with a red compass rose. Under it, timid men fight like pirates.

name: Aegis Cloak of the Hollow Legion
text: A legate's cloak with a bronze collar. The awakened legion's last oath was to guard whoever wore it.

name: Whisperless Chain
text: Lead links that drink sound. No spy hears what is said around it and no charm crosses it.
